title: Academic Archive
text:
My academic work has developed across engineering, scientific computing, cryptography, electronic documents, digital signatures, identity, post-quantum cryptography, and artificial intelligence.
This archive is not intended to reproduce a curriculum vitae. It is a historical view of how research questions, projects, technological artifacts, publications, students, and collaborations have evolved and intersected over time.

title: Talks
text:
Invited talks, conference presentations, panels, tutorials, workshops, and professional presentations form an important part of my academic and technical activity.
This archive is being reconstructed from curriculum records, institutional sources, event programs, and historical material. It records presentations for which there is documentary evidence; simple event attendance and academic-service activities are maintained separately.

title: Software & Data
text:
My research has produced software, technological platforms, digital infrastructures, prototypes, reference implementations, and other artifacts. This page preserves both current work and the technological history behind it.
The registry distinguishes research projects from the technological artifacts they produce. A project may generate several artifacts, while an artifact may connect multiple projects, publications, students, and institutions.

title: Software & Data
text:
Preservation Model
The long-term preservation strategy separates three layers:

Development — source code and active collaboration environments;
Publication — stable releases associated with papers, projects, and academic outputs;
Preservation — durable research objects with persistent metadata and, where appropriate, archival repositories and DOIs.

This structure is intended to preserve relationships such as:
project → software → release → dataset → publication → student → talk

title: Publications
text:
My publication record spans cryptography, public-key infrastructure, digital signatures, electronic documents, digital identity, post-quantum cryptography, and earlier research in computing, networks, and signal analysis.
The bibliography is organized around canonical scholarly works. A conference paper, journal version, preprint, or ePrint belonging to the same scholarly contribution is therefore consolidated as one work, while the individual bibliographic manifestations remain accessible.

title: Arquivo Acadêmico
text:
Meu trabalho acadêmico se desenvolveu entre engenharia, computação científica, criptografia, documentos eletrônicos, assinaturas digitais, identidade, criptografia pós-quântica e inteligência artificial.
Este arquivo não pretende reproduzir um currículo. Ele oferece uma visão histórica de como questões de pesquisa, projetos, artefatos tecnológicos, publicações, estudantes e colaborações evoluíram e se cruzaram ao longo do tempo.

title: Sobre
text:
Sou Professor Titular do Departamento de Informática e Estatística da Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC) e trabalho, há mais de três décadas, na interseção entre computação, criptografia e confiança digital.
Minha pesquisa atual concentra-se em segurança da informação e criptografia, particularmente assinaturas digitais, documentos eletrônicos, infraestruturas de chaves públicas, identidade eletrônica, credenciais verificáveis, gestão de chaves criptográficas, criptografia pós-quântica e aritmética de corpos finitos. Mais recentemente, também tenho investigado segurança, identidade, autorização e responsabilização de agentes de inteligência artificial.
Supervisiono o Laboratório de Segurança em Computação (LabSEC) da UFSC desde 2000, onde a pesquisa combina questões teóricas com o projeto e a implementação de infraestruturas de segurança e artefatos tecnológicos.

title: Sobre
text:
Formação acadêmica
Minha formação acadêmica começou em Engenharia Elétrica na UFSC, onde concluí a graduação em 1985. Posteriormente, concluí o mestrado em Engenharia Elétrica na UFSC em 1990, trabalhando com codificação paramétrica de sinais de voz com excitação multipulso.
Concluí o doutorado em Computação na Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) em 1999. Minha pesquisa de doutorado investigou análise não linear de padrões sonoros, com um estudo de caso envolvendo sons pulmonares.
Entre 2005 e 2006, realizei pós-doutorado na George Washington University, nos Estados Unidos.

title: Sobre
text:
Da engenharia à computação
Minha trajetória profissional começou na engenharia e na automação industrial. Entre 1986 e 1991, trabalhei na Fundação CERTI em pesquisa e desenvolvimento relacionados a sistemas de informação e automação industrial, incluindo responsabilidades de gestão na Divisão de Automação Industrial.
Em 1990–1991, passei um período no centro tecnológico Robotiker, na Espanha, trabalhando com robótica e automação industrial.
Ingressei na Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina (UDESC) como professor em 1992. Em 1994, ingressei na UFSC como docente permanente.

title: Sobre
text:
LabSEC e confiança digital
Na virada do milênio, minha pesquisa deslocou-se de forma decisiva para segurança da computação e criptografia. As atividades de pesquisa no LabSEC começaram em 2000, seguidas por minha supervisão do laboratório.
Os primeiros trabalhos abordaram documentos eletrônicos seguros, votação eletrônica, protocolos criptográficos, assinaturas digitais e infraestruturas de chaves públicas. Esses temas evoluíram para um programa de pesquisa mais amplo sobre os fundamentos tecnológicos da confiança digital.

title: Sobre
text:
Evolução da pesquisa
Uma forma de compreender minha pesquisa é como uma sequência de questões conectadas:
Como podemos tornar a computação confiável?
Essa questão apareceu inicialmente em meu trabalho por meio da criptografia, de protocolos seguros e de documentos eletrônicos. Posteriormente levou a assinaturas digitais e infraestruturas de chaves públicas, depois à identidade eletrônica e a novos modelos de credenciais e autenticação.
A segurança de longo prazo desses sistemas introduziu novas questões sobre criptografia pós-quântica, agilidade criptográfica, aritmética eficiente de corpos finitos e preservação de evidências eletrônicas.
A inteligência artificial introduz outra transição. Agentes autônomos e semiautônomos levantam questões familiares à segurança, mas sob nova forma: quem ou o que está agindo? Sob a autoridade de quem? Com quais credenciais? Como uma ação pode ser auditada, atribuída, autorizada ou repudiada?

title: Sobre
text:
Pesquisa e tecnologia
Sempre considerei protótipos de pesquisa e artefatos tecnológicos um complemento importante ao trabalho teórico e acadêmico.
Nos projetos do LabSEC, a pesquisa resultou em software e infraestrutura relacionados a documentos eletrônicos, assinaturas digitais, ICP/PKI, módulos criptográficos de hardware, gestão de certificados, identidade eletrônica, migração pós-quântica e serviços de registro civil.

title: Sobre
text:
Estudantes e comunidade de pesquisa
A orientação tem sido parte central do meu trabalho acadêmico. Pesquisas de mestrado e doutorado desenvolvidas no LabSEC contribuíram para muitas das linhas representadas neste site.
Em vez de tratar a orientação como uma atividade separada, considero os estudantes participantes de uma comunidade de pesquisa em continuidade.

title: Sobre
text:
Memória acadêmica
Este site também foi concebido como um arquivo acadêmico de longo prazo.
Publicações, isoladamente, oferecem uma visão incompleta de uma carreira de pesquisa. Projetos, software, textos técnicos, palestras, disciplinas, estudantes, colaborações e linhas de investigação inacabadas frequentemente explicam como as ideias se desenvolveram e como uma linha de pesquisa levou a outra.

Filosofia de Ensino
Entendo o ensino como uma conexão entre fundamentos formais e problemas computacionais reais. Em matemática, segurança, criptografia e inteligência artificial, os estudantes devem compreender não apenas como uma técnica funciona, mas também as premissas, limitações e consequências de seu uso.
Trabalhos práticos, leitura crítica, discussão e construção de protótipos funcionais complementam os fundamentos conceituais das disciplinas.

title: Research
text:
My research is concerned with a broad question: how can computation be made trustworthy?
Over time, this question has connected mathematical foundations, cryptographic mechanisms, electronic documents, digital signatures, public-key infrastructures, electronic identity, post-quantum cryptography, and, more recently, artificial-intelligence agents.
The research areas below are therefore not independent topics. They form a set of related problems around digital trust: how identities, actions, documents, credentials, and computational processes can be authenticated, authorized, protected, verified, preserved, and audited.

title: Research
text:
Research Foundations

Cryptography
Cryptography provides the technical foundation for much of my research.
My work has addressed cryptographic protocols and their applications to secure electronic transactions, digital signatures, authentication, electronic documents, voting systems, public-key infrastructures, and key-management systems.
A recurring concern is not only whether a cryptographic primitive is secure in isolation, but how it behaves when incorporated into a complete system involving people, software, hardware, institutions, and long-lived information.


Finite-Field Arithmetic
Efficient arithmetic over finite fields is an important foundation for cryptographic implementations.
Current work investigates polynomial-basis arithmetic over binary extension fields, particularly the selection and structure of irreducible polynomials and the cost of modular reduction. The objective is to understand how algebraic structure influences implementation cost, including the number of logical operations and circuit depth.
This line also explores computational methods for discovering and evaluating useful families of irreducible polynomials.

title: Research
text:
Digital Trust

Digital Signatures
Digital signatures have been one of the central themes of my research for more than two decades.
The work ranges from signature mechanisms and certificate infrastructures to signature policies, long-term signatures, user-centric signing models, and the relationship between a cryptographic signature and the electronic document or act that it represents.
A persistent research question is how digital evidence can remain verifiable as algorithms, certificates, software, and trust infrastructures evolve.


Public-Key Infrastructure
Public-key infrastructures connect cryptographic mechanisms to operational trust.
My research in PKI has included certificate management, certification architectures, hardware security modules, signature policies, educational PKIs, certificate validation, and the design of trust infrastructures.
This work has included both academic research and technological development in collaboration with Brazilian digital-trust initiatives.


Electronic Identity
Electronic identity extends the trust problem beyond certificates.
Current research considers authentication, identity management, attributes, authorization, verifiable credentials, and the relationship between an identity and the digital acts performed under that identity.
One objective is to develop architectures in which identity, authentication, signatures, attributes, and authorization can be composed without unnecessarily collapsing them into a single mechanism.


Electronic Documents
Electronic documents are not merely files. They are information objects whose authenticity, integrity, confidentiality, provenance, signatures, and evidentiary value may need to survive for long periods.
Research in this area includes secure document exchange, trusted timestamps, digital signatures, long-term preservation, confidentiality, cryptographic key management, and mechanisms for maintaining verifiability despite technological change.
This research has increasingly converged with electronic identity and post-quantum cryptography.

title: Research
text:
Emerging Directions

Post-Quantum Cryptography
The transition to post-quantum cryptography is not simply the replacement of one algorithm by another.
It affects certificate formats, protocols, hardware, key management, digital signatures, identity systems, software lifecycles, interoperability, and long-term electronic evidence.
My research therefore examines post-quantum migration as a systems problem, including hybrid mechanisms, legacy-system adaptation, electronic identity, certificates, network protocols, and the preservation of digitally signed information.


Artificial Intelligence & Security
Artificial intelligence creates both new security mechanisms and new security subjects.
AI can support security analysis, document processing, classification, and interaction with complex information systems. At the same time, autonomous and semi-autonomous agents introduce questions about identity, credentials, authorization, accountability, privacy, and auditability.
A current research direction investigates how an AI agent can be identified and authorized to perform consequential digital acts on behalf of a person or organization.
This connects emerging agentic systems to long-standing security concepts such as authentication, delegation, authorization, signatures, attributes, evidence, and non-repudiation.

title: Research
text:
Current Research Questions
Several questions currently connect these research areas:

AI agent identity and authority. How should an autonomous or semi-autonomous agent be identified, authenticated, and authorized when acting for a person or organization?
Accountable digital acts. What evidence should be produced when software or an AI agent performs an action with legal, financial, administrative, or security consequences?
Post-quantum transition. How can existing PKI, identity, document, and network infrastructures migrate to post-quantum cryptography without losing interoperability or historical evidence?
Long-term electronic evidence. How can electronic documents and signatures remain verifiable when algorithms, certificates, keys, software, and trust anchors change over decades?
Efficient finite-field arithmetic. Can structured families of irreducible polynomials reduce the implementation cost of arithmetic over binary extension fields?
Composable digital identity. How should identity, authentication, attributes, signatures, representation, delegation, and authorization interact in modern digital-trust architectures?
Sovereign and domain-specific AI. How can specialized AI systems operate over sensitive institutional knowledge while maintaining control over data, provenance, access, and accountability?

title: Research
text:
Research Approach
My research combines several levels of investigation:
Foundations. Mathematical structures, cryptographic algorithms, protocols, and security models.
Architectures. PKI, identity systems, electronic-document infrastructures, key-management systems, and AI-agent trust models.
Technological artifacts. Prototypes, reference implementations, software, and experimental infrastructures used to test research ideas.
Deployment and institutions. The interaction between technology, regulation, operational processes, usability, and real trust ecosystems.
This combination is deliberate. Security mechanisms that are correct in isolation may fail when embedded in larger sociotechnical systems. Conversely, practical infrastructure problems often expose research questions that are invisible at the level of individual algorithms.

title: Investigación
text:
Mi investigación se organiza alrededor de una pregunta amplia: ¿cómo podemos hacer que la computación sea confiable?
A lo largo del tiempo, esta pregunta ha conectado fundamentos matemáticos, mecanismos criptográficos, documentos electrónicos, firmas digitales, infraestructuras de clave pública, identidad electrónica, criptografía poscuántica y, más recientemente, agentes de inteligencia artificial.
Las áreas siguientes no son temas independientes. Forman un conjunto de problemas relacionados con la confianza digital: cómo identidades, acciones, documentos, credenciales y procesos computacionales pueden ser autenticados, autorizados, protegidos, verificados, preservados y auditados.

title: Investigación
text:
Fundamentos de la investigación

Criptografía
La criptografía proporciona la base técnica de gran parte de mi investigación. Mi trabajo aborda protocolos criptográficos y sus aplicaciones en transacciones electrónicas seguras, firmas digitales, autenticación, documentos electrónicos, sistemas de votación, PKI y gestión de claves.


Aritmética de cuerpos finitos
El trabajo actual investiga aritmética en base polinomial sobre extensiones binarias, especialmente la selección y estructura de polinomios irreducibles y el costo de la reducción modular.

title: Investigación
text:
Confianza digital

Firmas digitales
Las firmas digitales han sido uno de los temas centrales de mi investigación durante más de dos décadas. El trabajo incluye mecanismos de firma, infraestructuras de certificados, políticas de firma, firmas de largo plazo y modelos centrados en el usuario.


Infraestructura de Clave Pública
Mi investigación en PKI incluye gestión de certificados, arquitecturas de certificación, módulos criptográficos de hardware, políticas de firma, PKI académicas, validación de certificados e infraestructuras de confianza.


Identidad electrónica
La investigación actual considera autenticación, gestión de identidades, atributos, autorización, credenciales verificables y la relación entre una identidad y los actos digitales realizados bajo esa identidad.


Documentos electrónicos
Los documentos electrónicos no son simplemente archivos. Son objetos de información cuya autenticidad, integridad, confidencialidad, procedencia, firmas y valor probatorio pueden necesitar sobrevivir durante largos períodos.

title: Investigación
text:
Direcciones emergentes

Criptografía poscuántica
La transición a la criptografía poscuántica no consiste simplemente en sustituir un algoritmo por otro. Afecta formatos de certificados, protocolos, hardware, gestión de claves, firmas digitales, sistemas de identidad, ciclos de vida del software, interoperabilidad y evidencia electrónica a largo plazo.


Inteligencia Artificial y Seguridad
La inteligencia artificial crea nuevos mecanismos de seguridad y también nuevos sujetos de seguridad. Los agentes autónomos y semiautónomos introducen cuestiones sobre identidad, credenciales, autorización, responsabilidad, privacidad y auditabilidad.
Una línea actual investiga cómo un agente de IA puede ser identificado y autorizado para realizar actos digitales con consecuencias en nombre de una persona u organización.

title: Investigación
text:
Preguntas actuales de investigación

Identidad y autoridad de agentes de IA. ¿Cómo identificar, autenticar y autorizar agentes autónomos o semiautónomos?
Actos digitales atribuibles. ¿Qué evidencia debe producirse cuando software o IA realiza acciones con consecuencias?
Transición poscuántica. ¿Cómo migrar infraestructuras existentes sin perder interoperabilidad ni evidencia histórica?
Evidencia electrónica a largo plazo. ¿Cómo mantener documentos y firmas verificables durante décadas?
Aritmética eficiente de cuerpos finitos. ¿Pueden familias estructuradas de polinomios irreducibles reducir los costos de implementación?
Identidad digital componible. ¿Cómo deben interactuar identidad, autenticación, atributos, firmas, representación, delegación y autorización?
IA soberana y específica de dominio. ¿Cómo operar sobre conocimiento institucional sensible manteniendo control sobre datos, procedencia, acceso y responsabilidad?

La dirección académica es más que una lista de tesis. Representa el desarrollo de líneas de investigación, colaboraciones y sucesivas generaciones de investigadores.
Varios estudiantes inicialmente dirigidos en la maestría continuaron posteriormente sus estudios de doctorado, mientras que antiguos estudiantes se convirtieron en investigadores, profesores y directores académicos.
Se encuentra en desarrollo una genealogía académica estructurada que conecta estudiantes, publicaciones, proyectos, software y temas de investigación.

title: Conferencias
text:
Las conferencias invitadas, presentaciones en congresos, paneles, tutoriales, talleres y presentaciones profesionales constituyen una parte importante de mi actividad académica y técnica.
Este archivo se está reconstruyendo a partir de registros curriculares, fuentes institucionales, programas de eventos y material histórico. Registra presentaciones para las que existe evidencia documental; la simple asistencia a eventos y las actividades de servicio académico se mantienen por separado.

title: Libros y Textos
text:
Esta sección reúne libros, capítulos, textos técnicos y científicos, materiales docentes y trabajos profesionales seleccionados producidos a lo largo de mi carrera académica.
La colección se está reconstruyendo progresivamente a partir de registros bibliográficos y archivos históricos. Un registro bibliográfico confirma que una obra forma parte del registro académico; no significa necesariamente que exista actualmente una copia digital pública disponible.

text:
Mi investigación ha producido software, plataformas tecnológicas, infraestructuras digitales, prototipos, implementaciones de referencia y otros artefactos. Esta página preserva tanto el trabajo actual como la historia tecnológica que lo precede.

title: Software y Datos
text:
Modelo de Preservación
La estrategia de preservación a largo plazo separa tres capas:

Desarrollo — código fuente y entornos activos de colaboración;
Publicación — versiones estables asociadas con artículos, proyectos y resultados académicos;
Preservación — objetos de investigación duraderos, con metadatos persistentes y, cuando corresponda, repositorios de archivo y DOIs.

Esta estructura busca preservar relaciones como:
proyecto → software → versión → conjunto de datos → publicación → estudiante → conferencia

title: Teaching
text:
Teaching Philosophy
I approach teaching as a connection between formal foundations and real computational problems. In mathematics, security, cryptography, and artificial intelligence, students should understand not only how a technique works, but also the assumptions, limitations, and consequences of using it.
Practical work, critical reading, discussion, and the construction of working prototypes complement the conceptual foundations of the courses.

title: Projects
text:
My research has often been developed through long-term initiatives that connect fundamental research, technological development, infrastructure, standards, and real-world applications.
The portfolio spans cryptography, digital trust, electronic documents, digital identity, post-quantum security, artificial intelligence, and information infrastructures. Research programs represent continuing lines of investigation, while projects have more specific technological, scientific, or institutional objectives.

title: Projects
text:
From Research to Technology
A recurring objective of these initiatives is to connect foundational research with deployable systems, standards, open implementations, and long-term digital infrastructures. Some completed projects continue to influence current work, either through technologies reused in new projects or through research questions that evolved into continuing research programs.

Concibo la docencia como una conexión entre fundamentos formales y problemas computacionales reales. En matemáticas, seguridad, criptografía e inteligencia artificial, los estudiantes deben comprender no solo cómo funciona una técnica, sino también sus supuestos, limitaciones y consecuencias.
El trabajo práctico, la lectura crítica, la discusión y la construcción de prototipos funcionales complementan los fundamentos conceptuales de las asignaturas.

text:

title: Sobre mí
text:
Formación académica
Mi formación académica comenzó en Ingeniería Eléctrica en la UFSC, donde obtuve el título de grado en 1985. Posteriormente completé la maestría en Ingeniería Eléctrica en la UFSC en 1990, trabajando en codificación paramétrica de señales de voz con excitación multipulso.
Obtuve el doctorado en Computación en la Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) en 1999. Mi investigación doctoral estudió el análisis no lineal de patrones sonoros, con un estudio de caso sobre sonidos pulmonares.
Entre 2005 y 2006 realicé una estancia posdoctoral en George Washington University, Estados Unidos.

title: Sobre mí
section: De la ingeniería a la computación
text:
De la ingeniería a la computación
Mi trayectoria profesional comenzó en ingeniería y automatización industrial. Entre 1986 y 1991 trabajé en Fundação CERTI en investigación y desarrollo relacionados con sistemas de información y automatización industrial.
En 1990–1991 pasé un período en el centro tecnológico Robotiker, en España, trabajando con robótica y automatización industrial.
Me incorporé a la Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina (UDESC) como profesor en 1992 y a la UFSC como docente permanente en 1994.

title: Sobre mí
text:
LabSEC y confianza digital
Alrededor del cambio de milenio, mi investigación se orientó decisivamente hacia la seguridad informática y la criptografía. Las actividades de investigación en LabSEC comenzaron en 2000, seguidas por mi supervisión del laboratorio.
Los primeros trabajos abordaron documentos electrónicos seguros, votación electrónica, protocolos criptográficos, firmas digitales e infraestructuras de clave pública. Estos temas evolucionaron hacia un programa más amplio sobre los fundamentos tecnológicos de la confianza digital.

title: Sobre mí
text:
Evolución de la investigación
Una forma de comprender mi investigación es como una secuencia de preguntas conectadas:
¿Cómo podemos hacer que la computación sea confiable?
Esta pregunta apareció inicialmente a través de la criptografía, los protocolos seguros y los documentos electrónicos. Posteriormente condujo a firmas digitales y PKI, y después a identidad electrónica y nuevos modelos de credenciales y autenticación.
La seguridad a largo plazo introdujo nuevas cuestiones sobre criptografía poscuántica, agilidad criptográfica, aritmética eficiente de cuerpos finitos y preservación de evidencia electrónica.
La inteligencia artificial introduce otra transición. Los agentes autónomos y semiautónomos plantean preguntas conocidas para la seguridad bajo una nueva forma: ¿quién o qué actúa?, ¿bajo la autoridad de quién?, ¿con qué credenciales?, ¿cómo puede una acción ser auditada, atribuida, autorizada o repudiada?

title: Sobre mí
text:
Investigación y tecnología
Siempre he considerado los prototipos de investigación y los artefactos tecnológicos como un complemento importante del trabajo teórico y académico.
Los proyectos de LabSEC han producido software e infraestructura relacionados con documentos electrónicos, firmas digitales, PKI, módulos criptográficos de hardware, gestión de certificados, identidad electrónica, migración poscuántica y servicios de registro civil.

title: Sobre mí
text:
Estudiantes y comunidad de investigación
La dirección de estudiantes ha sido una parte central de mi trabajo académico. Las investigaciones de maestría y doctorado desarrolladas en LabSEC han contribuido a muchas de las líneas representadas en este sitio.

title: Sobre mí
text:
Memoria académica
Este sitio también está concebido como un archivo académico de largo plazo.
Las publicaciones por sí solas ofrecen una visión incompleta de una carrera de investigación. Los proyectos, el software, los textos técnicos, las charlas, los cursos, los estudiantes, las colaboraciones y las líneas de investigación inacabadas ayudan a documentar cómo evolucionan las ideas.

title: Archivo Académico
text:
Mi trabajo académico se ha desarrollado entre la ingeniería, la computación científica, la criptografía, los documentos electrónicos, las firmas digitales, la identidad, la criptografía poscuántica y la inteligencia artificial.
Este archivo no pretende reproducir un currículum. Ofrece una visión histórica de cómo las preguntas de investigación, los proyectos, los artefactos tecnológicos, las publicaciones, los estudiantes y las colaboraciones han evolucionado y se han cruzado a lo largo del tiempo.

Teaching Philosophy
I approach teaching as a connection between formal foundations and real computational problems. In mathematics, security, cryptography, and artificial intelligence, students should understand not only how a technique works, but also the assumptions, limitations, and consequences of using it.
Practical work, critical reading, discussion, and the construction of working prototypes complement the conceptual foundations of the courses.

My current research focuses on information security and cryptography, particularly digital signatures, electronic documents, public-key infrastructures, electronic identity, verifiable credentials, cryptographic key management, post-quantum cryptography, and finite-field arithmetic. title: About
text:
Academic Formation
My academic formation began in Electrical Engineering at UFSC, where I received my bachelor’s degree in 1985. I subsequently completed a master’s degree in Electrical Engineering at UFSC in 1990, working on parametric speech coding with multi-pulse excitation.
I received my PhD in Computer Science from the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) in 1999. My doctoral research investigated nonlinear analysis of sound patterns, with a case study involving lung sounds.
From 2005 to 2006, I was a postdoctoral researcher at George Washington University in the United States.

title: About
text:
From Engineering to Computing
My professional trajectory began in engineering and industrial automation. From 1986 to 1991, I worked at Fundação CERTI in research and development related to information systems and industrial automation, including management responsibilities in the Industrial Automation Division.
In 1990–1991, I spent a period at the Robotiker technology center in Spain working with industrial robotics and automation.
I joined the Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina (UDESC) as a professor in 1992. There, my research already included cryptography and its applications.
In 1994, I joined UFSC as a permanent faculty member. My initial research at the Department of Informatics and Statistics was associated with computational mathematics and the Laboratory of Algebraic and Symbolic Computing.

title: About
text:
LabSEC and Digital Trust
Around the turn of the millennium, my research shifted decisively toward computer security and cryptography. Research activities at LabSEC began in 2000, followed by my supervision of the laboratory.
Early research addressed secure electronic documents, electronic voting, cryptographic protocols, digital signatures, and public-key infrastructures. These themes developed into a broader research program concerned with the technological foundations of digital trust.
Over the following decades, this work expanded to certificate lifecycle management, hardware security modules, long-term digital signatures, secure document preservation, authentication, electronic identity, and national-scale trust infrastructures.
My work has also involved collaboration with Brazilian digital-trust initiatives. I coordinated the ICP-EDU working group of the Brazilian National Research and Education Network (RNP) and have participated in activities associated with ICP-Brasil.

title: About
text:
Research Evolution
A useful way to understand my research is as a sequence of connected questions:
How can computation be made trustworthy?
That question first appeared in my work through cryptography, secure protocols, and electronic documents. It subsequently led to digital signatures and public-key infrastructures, then to electronic identity and new models for credentials and authentication.
The long-term security of these systems introduced further questions about post-quantum cryptography, cryptographic agility, efficient finite-field arithmetic, and preservation of electronic evidence.
Artificial intelligence introduces another transition. Autonomous and semi-autonomous agents raise questions that are familiar to security research but appear in a new form: Who or what is acting? Under whose authority? With which credentials? How can an action be audited, attributed, authorized, or repudiated?
These questions currently connect my earlier work on digital trust with research on AI agents and personal AI.

title: About
text:
Research and Technology
I have always considered research prototypes and technological artifacts an important complement to theoretical and academic work.
Across LabSEC projects, research has resulted in software and infrastructure related to electronic documents, digital signatures, PKI, hardware security modules, certificate management, electronic identity, post-quantum migration, and civil-registration services.
The Projects and Software & Data sections document this technological trajectory in greater detail.

title: About
text:
Students and Research Community
Supervision has been a central part of my academic work. Master’s and doctoral research conducted at LabSEC has contributed to many of the research lines represented on this site, including electronic documents, cryptographic protocols, PKI, digital signatures, identity, post-quantum cryptography, and finite-field arithmetic.
Rather than treating supervision as a separate activity, I regard students as participants in a continuing research community. The Supervision section preserves this academic genealogy.

title: Pesquisa
text:
Minha pesquisa está organizada em torno de uma questão ampla: como podemos tornar a computação confiável?
Ao longo do tempo, essa questão conectou fundamentos matemáticos, mecanismos criptográficos, documentos eletrônicos, assinaturas digitais, infraestruturas de chaves públicas, identidade eletrônica, criptografia pós-quântica e, mais recentemente, agentes de inteligência artificial.
As áreas abaixo não são temas independentes. Elas formam um conjunto de problemas relacionados à confiança digital: como identidades, ações, documentos, credenciais e processos computacionais podem ser autenticados, autorizados, protegidos, verificados, preservados e auditados.

title: Pesquisa
text:
Fundamentos da pesquisa

Criptografia
A criptografia fornece a base técnica para grande parte da minha pesquisa. Meu trabalho aborda protocolos criptográficos e suas aplicações em transações eletrônicas seguras, assinaturas digitais, autenticação, documentos eletrônicos, sistemas de votação, ICP/PKI e gestão de chaves.


Aritmética de corpos finitos
O trabalho atual investiga aritmética em base polinomial sobre extensões binárias, particularmente a seleção e a estrutura de polinômios irredutíveis e o custo da redução modular.

title: Pesquisa
text:
Confiança digital

Assinaturas digitais
As assinaturas digitais constituem um dos temas centrais da minha pesquisa há mais de duas décadas. O trabalho inclui mecanismos de assinatura, infraestruturas de certificados, políticas de assinatura, assinaturas de longo prazo e modelos de assinatura centrados no usuário.


Infraestrutura de Chaves Públicas
Minha pesquisa em ICP/PKI inclui gestão de certificados, arquiteturas de certificação, módulos criptográficos de hardware, políticas de assinatura, ICPs acadêmicas, validação de certificados e projeto de infraestruturas de confiança.


Identidade eletrônica
A pesquisa atual considera autenticação, gestão de identidades, atributos, autorização, credenciais verificáveis e a relação entre uma identidade e os atos digitais realizados sob essa identidade.


Documentos eletrônicos
Documentos eletrônicos não são apenas arquivos. São objetos de informação cuja autenticidade, integridade, confidencialidade, proveniência, assinaturas e valor probatório podem precisar sobreviver por longos períodos.

title: Pesquisa
text:
Direções emergentes

Criptografia pós-quântica
A transição para a criptografia pós-quântica não é apenas a substituição de um algoritmo por outro. Ela afeta formatos de certificados, protocolos, hardware, gestão de chaves, assinaturas digitais, sistemas de identidade, ciclos de vida de software, interoperabilidade e evidências eletrônicas de longo prazo.


Inteligência Artificial e Segurança
A inteligência artificial cria novos mecanismos de segurança e também novos sujeitos de segurança. Agentes autônomos e semiautônomos introduzem questões sobre identidade, credenciais, autorização, responsabilização, privacidade e auditabilidade.
Uma direção atual investiga como um agente de IA pode ser identificado e autorizado a realizar atos digitais consequenciais em nome de uma pessoa ou organização.

title: Pesquisa
text:
Questões atuais de pesquisa

Identidade e autoridade de agentes de IA. Como identificar, autenticar e autorizar agentes autônomos ou semiautônomos?
Atos digitais responsabilizáveis. Que evidências devem ser produzidas quando software ou IA realiza ações com consequências?
Transição pós-quântica. Como migrar infraestruturas existentes sem perder interoperabilidade ou evidências históricas?
Evidências eletrônicas de longo prazo. Como manter documentos e assinaturas verificáveis durante décadas?
Aritmética eficiente de corpos finitos. Famílias estruturadas de polinômios irredutíveis podem reduzir custos de implementação?
Identidade digital componível. Como identidade, autenticação, atributos, assinaturas, representação, delegação e autorização devem interagir?
IA soberana e específica de domínio. Como operar sobre conhecimento institucional sensível mantendo controle sobre dados, proveniência, acesso e responsabilização?

title: Research
text:
My research is concerned with a broad question: how can computation be made trustworthy?
Over time, this question has connected mathematical foundations, cryptographic mechanisms, electronic documents, digital signatures, public-key infrastructures, electronic identity, post-quantum cryptography, and, more recently, artificial-intelligence agents.
The research areas below are therefore not independent topics. They form a set of related problems around digital trust: how identities, actions, documents, credentials, and computational processes can be authenticated, authorized, protected, verified, preserved, and audited.

title: Research
text:
Research Foundations

Cryptography
Cryptography provides the technical foundation for much of my research.
My work has addressed cryptographic protocols and their applications to secure electronic transactions, digital signatures, authentication, electronic documents, voting systems, public-key infrastructures, and key-management systems.
A recurring concern is not only whether a cryptographic primitive is secure in isolation, but how it behaves when incorporated into a complete system involving people, software, hardware, institutions, and long-lived information.


Finite-Field Arithmetic
Efficient arithmetic over finite fields is an important foundation for cryptographic implementations.
Current work investigates polynomial-basis arithmetic over binary extension fields, particularly the selection and structure of irreducible polynomials and the cost of modular reduction. The objective is to understand how algebraic structure influences implementation cost, including the number of logical operations and circuit depth.
This line also explores computational methods for discovering and evaluating useful families of irreducible polynomials.

title: Research
text:
Digital Trust

Digital Signatures
Digital signatures have been one of the central themes of my research for more than two decades.
The work ranges from signature mechanisms and certificate infrastructures to signature policies, long-term signatures, user-centric signing models, and the relationship between a cryptographic signature and the electronic document or act that it represents.
A persistent research question is how digital evidence can remain verifiable as algorithms, certificates, software, and trust infrastructures evolve.


Public-Key Infrastructure
Public-key infrastructures connect cryptographic mechanisms to operational trust.
My research in PKI has included certificate management, certification architectures, hardware security modules, signature policies, educational PKIs, certificate validation, and the design of trust infrastructures.
This work has included both academic research and technological development in collaboration with Brazilian digital-trust initiatives.


Electronic Identity
Electronic identity extends the trust problem beyond certificates.
Current research considers authentication, identity management, attributes, authorization, verifiable credentials, and the relationship between an identity and the digital acts performed under that identity.
One objective is to develop architectures in which identity, authentication, signatures, attributes, and authorization can be composed without unnecessarily collapsing them into a single mechanism.


Electronic Documents
Electronic documents are not merely files. They are information objects whose authenticity, integrity, confidentiality, provenance, signatures, and evidentiary value may need to survive for long periods.
Research in this area includes secure document exchange, trusted timestamps, digital signatures, long-term preservation, confidentiality, cryptographic key management, and mechanisms for maintaining verifiability despite technological change.
This research has increasingly converged with electronic identity and post-quantum cryptography.

title: Research
text:
Emerging Directions

Post-Quantum Cryptography
The transition to post-quantum cryptography is not simply the replacement of one algorithm by another.
It affects certificate formats, protocols, hardware, key management, digital signatures, identity systems, software lifecycles, interoperability, and long-term electronic evidence.
My research therefore examines post-quantum migration as a systems problem, including hybrid mechanisms, legacy-system adaptation, electronic identity, certificates, network protocols, and the preservation of digitally signed information.


Artificial Intelligence & Security
Artificial intelligence creates both new security mechanisms and new security subjects.
AI can support security analysis, document processing, classification, and interaction with complex information systems. At the same time, autonomous and semi-autonomous agents introduce questions about identity, credentials, authorization, accountability, privacy, and auditability.
A current research direction investigates how an AI agent can be identified and authorized to perform consequential digital acts on behalf of a person or organization.
This connects emerging agentic systems to long-standing security concepts such as authentication, delegation, authorization, signatures, attributes, evidence, and non-repudiation.

title: Research
text:
Current Research Questions
Several questions currently connect these research areas:

AI agent identity and authority. How should an autonomous or semi-autonomous agent be identified, authenticated, and authorized when acting for a person or organization?
Accountable digital acts. What evidence should be produced when software or an AI agent performs an action with legal, financial, administrative, or security consequences?
Post-quantum transition. How can existing PKI, identity, document, and network infrastructures migrate to post-quantum cryptography without losing interoperability or historical evidence?
Long-term electronic evidence. How can electronic documents and signatures remain verifiable when algorithms, certificates, keys, software, and trust anchors change over decades?
Efficient finite-field arithmetic. Can structured families of irreducible polynomials reduce the implementation cost of arithmetic over binary extension fields?
Composable digital identity. How should identity, authentication, attributes, signatures, representation, delegation, and authorization interact in modern digital-trust architectures?
Sovereign and domain-specific AI. How can specialized AI systems operate over sensitive institutional knowledge while maintaining control over data, provenance, access, and accountability?

title: Research
text:
Research Approach
My research combines several levels of investigation:
Foundations. Mathematical structures, cryptographic algorithms, protocols, and security models.
Architectures. PKI, identity systems, electronic-document infrastructures, key-management systems, and AI-agent trust models.
Technological artifacts. Prototypes, reference implementations, software, and experimental infrastructures used to test research ideas.
Deployment and institutions. The interaction between technology, regulation, operational processes, usability, and real trust ecosystems.
This combination is deliberate. Security mechanisms that are correct in isolation may fail when embedded in larger sociotechnical systems. Conversely, practical infrastructure problems often expose research questions that are invisible at the level of individual algorithms.

title: About
text:
I am a Full Professor in the Department of Informatics and Statistics at the Federal University of Santa Catarina (UFSC), Brazil, and have worked at the intersection of computing, cryptography, and digital trust for more than three decades.
My current research focuses on information security and cryptography, particularly digital signatures, electronic documents, public-key infrastructures, electronic identity, verifiable credentials, cryptographic key management, post-quantum cryptography, and finite-field arithmetic. More recently, I have also been investigating security, identity, authorization, and accountability for artificial-intelligence agents.
I have supervised the Laboratory for Computer Security (LabSEC) at UFSC since 2000, where research has combined theoretical questions with the design and implementation of security infrastructures and technological artifacts.

title: About
text:
Academic Formation
My academic formation began in Electrical Engineering at UFSC, where I received my bachelor’s degree in 1985. I subsequently completed a master’s degree in Electrical Engineering at UFSC in 1990, working on parametric speech coding with multi-pulse excitation.
I received my PhD in Computer Science from the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) in 1999. My doctoral research investigated nonlinear analysis of sound patterns, with a case study involving lung sounds.
From 2005 to 2006, I was a postdoctoral researcher at George Washington University in the United States.

title: About
text:
From Engineering to Computing
My professional trajectory began in engineering and industrial automation. From 1986 to 1991, I worked at Fundação CERTI in research and development related to information systems and industrial automation, including management responsibilities in the Industrial Automation Division.
In 1990–1991, I spent a period at the Robotiker technology center in Spain working with industrial robotics and automation.
I joined the Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina (UDESC) as a professor in 1992. There, my research already included cryptography and its applications.
In 1994, I joined UFSC as a permanent faculty member. My initial research at the Department of Informatics and Statistics was associated with computational mathematics and the Laboratory of Algebraic and Symbolic Computing.

title: About
text:
LabSEC and Digital Trust
Around the turn of the millennium, my research shifted decisively toward computer security and cryptography. Research activities at LabSEC began in 2000, followed by my supervision of the laboratory.
Early research addressed secure electronic documents, electronic voting, cryptographic protocols, digital signatures, and public-key infrastructures. These themes developed into a broader research program concerned with the technological foundations of digital trust.
Over the following decades, this work expanded to certificate lifecycle management, hardware security modules, long-term digital signatures, secure document preservation, authentication, electronic identity, and national-scale trust infrastructures.
My work has also involved collaboration with Brazilian digital-trust initiatives. I coordinated the ICP-EDU working group of the Brazilian National Research and Education Network (RNP) and have participated in activities associated with ICP-Brasil.

title: About
text:
Research Evolution
A useful way to understand my research is as a sequence of connected questions:
How can computation be made trustworthy?
That question first appeared in my work through cryptography, secure protocols, and electronic documents. It subsequently led to digital signatures and public-key infrastructures, then to electronic identity and new models for credentials and authentication.
The long-term security of these systems introduced further questions about post-quantum cryptography, cryptographic agility, efficient finite-field arithmetic, and preservation of electronic evidence.
Artificial intelligence introduces another transition. Autonomous and semi-autonomous agents raise questions that are familiar to security research but appear in a new form: Who or what is acting? Under whose authority? With which credentials? How can an action be audited, attributed, authorized, or repudiated?
These questions currently connect my earlier work on digital trust with research on AI agents and personal AI.

title: About
text:
Research and Technology
I have always considered research prototypes and technological artifacts an important complement to theoretical and academic work.
Across LabSEC projects, research has resulted in software and infrastructure related to electronic documents, digital signatures, PKI, hardware security modules, certificate management, electronic identity, post-quantum migration, and civil-registration services.
The Projects and Software & Data sections document this technological trajectory in greater detail.

title: About
text:
Students and Research Community
Supervision has been a central part of my academic work. Master’s and doctoral research conducted at LabSEC has contributed to many of the research lines represented on this site, including electronic documents, cryptographic protocols, PKI, digital signatures, identity, post-quantum cryptography, and finite-field arithmetic.
Rather than treating supervision as a separate activity, I regard students as participants in a continuing research community. The Supervision section preserves this academic genealogy.

title: About

Academic Memory
This website is also intended as a long-term academic archive.
Publications alone provide an incomplete account of a research career. Projects, software, technical texts, lectures, courses, students, collaborations, and unfinished research directions often explain how ideas developed and how one line of investigation led to another.
The Academic Archive therefore connects these different kinds of records and provides a historical view of my work.
